standard_prerequisites.name: n-connected function
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function f:A->B is n-connected when the n-truncation of each fibre is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property transferred between f and the map phi on total spaces.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibre-wise n-connected family
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family g:prod_{a:A} P(a)->Q(f(a)) is fibre-wise n-connected when each g_a is n-connected.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the extra hypothesis on the family over f.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation of a fibre and contractibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: trunc n (hfib h y) is contractible exactly when h is n-connected at y, and contractibility is a mere proposition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the form in which the equivalences of the proof are used, and the reason a merely inhabited fibre suffices.

core_obligations: For b:B and v:Q(b), compute trunc n (hfib phi (b,v)) as an iterated sum over w:hfib f b and u:P(proj1 w), and rewrite it by the fibre of g(proj1 w) (source lines 1279-1287).

Collapse the inner n-truncation inside the outer one, which is legitimate because trunc n of a type is an n-type, and so obtain that trunc n (hfib phi (b,v)) is equivalent to trunc n (hfib f b) (source lines 1285-1289).
Read the forward implication from the equivalence: if f is n-connected then every trunc n (hfib f b) is contractible, hence so is every trunc n (hfib phi (b,v)) (source line 1291).

For the converse, use the equivalence to transfer contractibility back along any b:B that has a v:Q(b), and finish by noticing that contractibility of trunc n (hfib f b) is a mere proposition, so it suffices to have v merely (source lines 1292-1293).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the n-truncated fibre of phi over (b,v) with an iterated sum and then with the n-truncated fibre of f over b.
Observe that contractibility transfers in both directions along that equivalence.
Derive the two implications, using that the conclusion is a mere proposition in the converse direction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.5.12 at source lines 1265-1276: for f:A->B, families P over A and Q over B and a fibre-wise n-connected family g:P(a)->Q(f(a)), the induced map phi on total spaces is n-connected if f is, and conversely if phi is n-connected and Q is fibre-wise merely inhabited then f itself is. The author's proof (source lines 1278-1294) is not a formal consequence of the neighbouring postcomposition criterion: it computes the n-truncated fibre of phi over (b,v) as a nested sum, uses that the inner n-truncation can be absorbed because trunc n of a type is an n-type so that the sum becomes exactly trunc n (hfib f b), and then observes that contractibility transfers both ways; the converse is where the merely-inhabited hypothesis enters, through the fact that contractibility of a truncation is a mere proposition.

compared.difference: Hypothesis and conclusion both differ. The neighbour counts the postcomposition criterion: for a family Q over B and f n-connected, the map of dependent function types is n-connected. The present lemma adds a fibre-wise n-connected family g:P(a)->Q(f(a)) over f, concludes n-connectedness of the induced map on total spaces sum P -> sum Q rather than of a function type, and its converse needs the extra hypothesis that Q is fibre-wise merely inhabited. Neither statement implies the other, so both are counted.
That item counts functoriality of the cone construction in section 7.4; the present lemma belongs to section 7.5 and shares no retained range with it.
